subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Efficiency: Why No Machine Is Perfect
description: A micro-lesson that makes Efficiency: Why No Machine Is Perfect usable.

hook.text: Every machine wastes energy. A car engine turns only 30% of fuel energy into motion. The rest becomes heat.

buildup.text: Efficiency is useful output divided by total input. A 90% efficient motor wastes 10% as heat and sound.

discovery.text: Friction, air resistance, and vibration steal energy at every stage. More parts mean more losses.

twist.text: Compound machines multiply both advantage and loss. Each additional stage adds friction to the chain.

climax.text: Engineers spend careers shaving fractions of a percent. In a power plant, 1% efficiency saves millions.

punchline.text: Perfection is impossible. Getting closer is the entire job.

quiz.question: Why do compound machines lose more energy than simple ones?
options: Their materials are weaker and absorb more kinetic energy
Each additional stage adds friction losses to the system
They operate at higher temperatures that destroy energy faster
